background.x: The high banks of the Path River are riddled with natural cave systems that, since ancient times, have been sites of spiritual importance to the peoples of Ustalav, Lastwall, and Belkzen. Grayce itself grew up around one such site, a shrine to the goddess Pharasma, but in other locations more sinister forces held sway. Centuries ago, a coven of hags gathered in a cave along a stretch of the Path River known today as the Shivering Bluffs. There, the hags made pacts with entities from beyond the Universe, including—or so it is rumored—the Netherworld. During the Shining Crusade, the forces of the Knights of Ozem scattered this coven, but the hags’ shadow still looms over the region.

Though many of the tales regarding the Shivering Bluffs are nothing but superstition, the area’s reputation for danger is well deserved. Few people visit the Bluffs, making them a haven for wild animals, and in the cave where the coven of hags once gathered, a tear in the fabric of reality occasionally allows even stranger creatures to pass through. The most infamous of these creatures is the Path River Peeler. Descriptions of the Peeler vary, but all agree it is an otherworldly monster that preys on the flocks of sheep that graze along the Bluffs’ fertile, eastern slopes. While sightings of the Peeler ebb and wane—sometimes whole generations pass without a single attack—in recent weeks the monster has become increasingly active. This, combined with other strange happenings that have occurred in Grayce of late, has put the entire town on edge.

One of Grayce’s least popular residents, a changeling named **Damarys** (spiteful female changeling witch 3), has seized this opportunity to stir up trouble in town. Abandoned as an infant on the doorstep of the temple of Grandmother Crow, Damarys has long felt like an outsider among the people of Grayce. This alienation grew stronger shortly after her 12th birthday, when voices claiming to be the spirits of the hags banished centuries before led Damarys to the Shivering Bluffs. There, in the darkest of the caves, the voices promised Damarys that if she were to bring ill fortune to the town of Grayce, one day a portal to her home—her true home—would be opened.

Excited by the thought of leaving Grayce behind, Damarys moved from the temple where she’d been raised to the countryside. Here, she could keep to herself and earn her living as a shepherd while remaining close to the Shivering Bluffs. She visited the hags’ cave often, and several weeks ago she noticed a thin crack forming in one of the cavern’s walls. On the chill wind that blew from the fissure, Damarys once again heard the whispers of the hags promising to bring her home. That night, Damarys awoke to find a monstrous creature crouched above her bed: a thing that seemed part monkey and part bat, but which walked upright like a human. The creature did no harm to Damarys, but the very next day, fresh reports of Grayce’s local cryptid, the Path River Peeler, began.

Damarys senses that her otherworldly patrons are about to make good on their promise. The crack from which the Peeler emerged grows wider, and Damarys believes that if she can keep the cryptid safe, a doorway to the Netherworld will be opened for her. In the meantime, she hopes to cause as much misery in Grayce as possible, exacting revenge for both herself and the voices she’s come to think of as her true family.

start.x: The adventure begins shortly after the PCs arrive in Grayce from their previous adventures. Give the PCs a chance to take care of any business they might have and to get a feel for the town, describing the settlement’s general layout and its more notable landmarks. Then—perhaps as the PCs are purchasing supplies at Grayce General Goods or securing rooms at the Ash Inn or Riverbend Tavern & Inn—they’re approached by **Albin Derkensoor** (old and hardy male human rancher 3). Albin is in his sixties, and his family moved to Grayce when he was still a child. Normally, Albin’s eyes twinkle with cheer, but today his wrinkled face is a mask of worry.

x: “Folks have been saying there’s adventurers in town, and by the looks of you, they’re right. If that’s true, I could surely use your help. I’ll buy you a drink and tell you all about it, if you’re interested.”

start.x: Assuming the PCs agree to hear Albin’s story, he directs them to the Sing-A-Long Bar. As he does, attempt a secret DC 12 Perception check to Sense Motive for each of the PCs. Any character who succeeds notes that while the people of Grayce clearly recognize Albin, they seem to be giving him the cold shoulder, casting suspicious looks in his direction, or even outright turning their backs on him. Albin endures this treatment silently and, when they arrive at the tavern, motions for the PCs to take a seat in a quiet corner (a rarity for this establishment once night falls). Once everyone is settled, he begins.

x: “Three nights ago, round about midnight, I was awakened by the worst sound I’ve heard in all my years. It was some sort of beast—of that I’m sure—but the cry it made was more like a laugh than a growl. A low chuckle, from deep in the throat, but louder than a peal of thunder.

“The sound was still echoing off the hills when my sheep began to scream. I rushed outside to find Euphis, my ranch hand, standing inside their pen hollering and beating on a shield. Once he’d calmed down, Euphis said he’d seen a monster bearing down on the flock. He managed to scare the thing off, but not before getting a good look at it. It was taller than you or me, even hunched over, and had eyes that burned like torches in the moonlight. The Path River Peeler, he swears it was.”

At this point, Albin holds up his calloused hands. “Now, Euphis is brave for certain, and I’d never question his word. But he’s not the brightest guy. I can’t say for sure what he saw. All I know is that my sheep are too frightened to graze their normal pastures. And I can’t forget that laugh.” Albin shakes his head. “If that thing wasn’t the Peeler, it was something just as bad, or worse.”

start.x: The PCs probably have questions about Albin’s story. Some likely inquiries, as well as Albin’s answers, follow.

**What’s the Path River Peeler?** At this, Albin smiles nervously. “A story told to scare the children, or so I thought until three days ago. Supposedly, it haunts the hills just north of town. No one agrees what the creature is, and truth be told, no one’s claimed to have seen it since I was young. But with all the trouble in town recently, word about what Euphis saw has spread.”

**Trouble? Like what?** “Well, that sinkhole, for one! It opened a week before my sheep got all stirred up. I don’t know what a hole in the ground has to do with the Peeler, but anything out of the ordinary makes folk nervous in these parts. And frightened people start making connections where there’s none to be had.” (In this, Albin is correct: the sinkhole has nothing to do with the Path River Peeler, though it does play a part in other adventures in this anthology, such as “Sabotage!” and “They Hunger Below.”)

**Why’s everyone giving you the cold shoulder?** “I can’t say I blame them,” Albin sighs. “If it was the Peeler Euphis saw, then maybe a curse has befallen me. Some say the Peeler brings pestilence with it, too. If that’s true, and my sheep have been infected, I couldn’t ask anyone to join my flock with theirs, not until this trouble’s been sorted out.”

**What can we do to help?** A look of determination settles on Albin’s face. “Find the Peeler—or whatever that creature was—and put it down. You can come to my place to look for tracks, but I’d start here in town if I were you. Maybe someone knows something about the Peeler—or has even seen the beast themselves and are just too scared to speak up.”

**Can we talk to Euphis about his experience?** “Well, of course you can. If you decide to help me out and take on this task, you can come by the farm and ask Euphis as much as you want. I told you everything he already told me, but he might remember some other helpful clue if asked the right questions.” Albin pauses for a moment and knits his brown slightly before continuing. “Like I told you, he’s a good guy, but a bit naive. I only ask that you are kind to him. He’s been through a lot.”

Albin isn’t wealthy, but he offers the party a total of 40 gp as a reward for tracking down the Path River Peeler. He also says the PCs are welcome to stay at his ranch until the matter’s settled. If the PCs agree, Albin heads home to prepare space for them to settle in once their investigations in town are finished.

grayce.x: Following Albin’s advice, the PCs can canvas Grayce for more information about the Path River Peeler, perhaps starting with the other patrons in the Sing-A-Long. As the PCs ask around, they quickly discover that while everyone in town has a story about the Peeler, most are little more than fairy tales passed down from parents or grandparents. No one living in Grayce today claims to have seen the monster firsthand—except, of course, Albin’s ranch hand Euphis.
For every 30 minutes the PCs spend asking about the Path River Peeler, one of them can attempt a DC 15 Diplomacy check to Gather Information.

tiers.x: On a critical success to Gather Information, the PCs learn about two of these leads rather than just one.
On a success, the PCs are directed to one of the three more substantive leads listed below.
Because current knowledge of the Peeler is only speculation, even on a failed check the PCs should learn one or more of the rumors listed in the Rumors in Grayce sidebar.

items: Jarelle Quaine, a ranger who patrols the pastures north of Grayce, is well respected in town. All agree that if anyone has solid information about the Peeler, it’s her.
Titus Horvat is a retired farmer turned amateur cryptozoologist and has been stirring up fears by telling wild stories about the Peeler.

Damarys is a shepherd who lives alone in a cottage just an hour’s walk from Albin’s ranch. No one in town has anything nice to say about Damarys, and more than one person is certain she has something to do with the Peeler’s sudden reappearance.

grayce.x: The PCs can follow up the leads in any order, and Jarelle, Titus, and Damarys might direct the party to each other if the PCs don’t discover all the leads themselves.

grayce.title: Rumors in Grayce
grayce.x: As the PCs ask around for information about the Path River Peeler, they hear no end of stories about the monster. It seems everyone in Grayce has a friend or relative who’s spotted the Peeler along a lonely road one night, though no one claims to have seen the beast themselves. What’s more, little tragedies like a child taking ill, random accidents, and even poor weather are often blamed on the Peeler, with no evidence to support the claim. Most describe the Peeler as a black-furred, bat-faced monster that walks upright, but the details vary from person to person.

The PCs might hear any of the following rumors during their investigation. As none of these claims are entirely true (and are some outright fabrications), the PCs don’t need to learn any of them to continue the adventure.

items: The Path River Peeler earns its name from the state in which it leaves its victims, who are often found stripped entirely of skin. It preys mostly on sheep but has also been known to hunt other animals—and people.
The monster hates loud noises. Singing at full volume is a surefire way to keep the beast at bay.
The Peeler lives in a cave somewhere in the Shivering Bluffs north of town. It retreats there every morning, lest the sun’s rays burn it to cinders.
If you see a patch of dark fungus, that’s a sign the Peeler has passed that way recently.
Nothing can harm the Path River Peeler, save fire.

The Path River Peeler is a devil summoned to the Universe by a coven of hags centuries ago. Though the hags are long gone, the Peeler still haunts the Shivering Bluffs, waiting for a chance to avenge its masters.

jarelle.x: **Jarelle Quaine** (upstanding female human ranger 1) has lived in Grayce her entire life and is well liked by nearly everyone in town. She’s especially respected by the shepherds who graze their flocks outside of town, as Jarelle regularly patrols the pastures to keep them free of wolves and other predators. When her parents both died several years ago, Jarelle was thrust into the role of sole caregiver for her younger sister, **Phara** (troublemaking female human teenager 0). Since then, the two have lived together in a cottage a few minutes outside of town.

When the PCs arrive, they find Jarelle busy oiling her bow, while Phara lounges in the branches of a nearby tree with one leg dangling and swinging back and forth, looking bored. As the PCs approach, Phara clambers from the tree and greets the party with an excited grin, eager to have new and interesting people to talk to. She peppers them with questions (“Are you adventurers?” “What monsters have you killed?” “Can you show me some magic?”), but it’s not long before Jarelle intervenes to ask the PCs their business.

If the PCs question Jarelle about the Path River Peeler, the young ranger nods matter-of-factly. Jarelle doesn’t typically take tall tales seriously, but she’s heard enough stories about the Peeler that she believes the monster’s not entirely a myth. She’s never seen the Peeler—and suspects that most people who claim to haven’t either—but she knows the wildness around Grayce is full of creatures far stranger than the wolves or occasional kobold or bugbear she encounters on her forays. To that end, she’s been keeping an eye out for the Peeler, but she also believes one shouldn’t go out of one’s way to look for trouble. “In my experience,” she says, “Trouble finds you soon enough. No reason to rush it.”

Though Jarelle believes Grayce’s best course of action is to simply wait and hope the Peeler moves on (like it always has for as long as people have been seeing the creature in these parts), she agrees to show the PCs her maps of the surrounding area and help them identify the best place to stake out the beast. All the while, Phara continues to interrupt, asking the PCs what they think the Peeler is, how they plan to kill it, and whether she can accompany them on their “Peeler hunt.”

Any PC can help Jarelle study her maps by succeeding at a DC 16 Survival or DC 14 Scouting Lore check. Another PC can Aid the check by making a successful DC 15 Deception, Diplomacy, or Performance check to distract Phara during the meeting.

tiers.x: On a success, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks made to overcome the obstacles in **Event 2: Countryside Chase**, as their familiarity with the area gives them an edge.
Even on a failure, Jarelle suggests a location where the PCs could start their hunt.

jarelle.x: As the PCs prepare to leave, Phara asks if she can come with when they kill the Peeler. At this, Jarelle puts her foot down: Though she’s certain her sister will make a fine ranger herself someday, she’s still too young to be hunting monsters, even accompanied by the PCs. Phara opens her mouth as if to protest but grudgingly accepts her older sister’s decision—at least for now. The PCs will meet Phara again when she disguises herself as the Path River Peeler during **Event 2**.

jarelle.title: Reward
jarelle.x: For helping Jarelle identify the best place to stake out the Peeler, grant the PCs 20 XP.

titus.x: **Titus Horvat** (credulous nonbinary human cryptozoologist 2) was a struggling farmer when they received a surprise inheritance from their uncle, a professor of biology at the University of Lepidstadt. The estate included a modest library, as well as hundreds of their uncle’s journals, each filled with sketches of unusual creatures that had been dissected at the university. Their imagination inflamed by these images, Titus immediately retired from farming to pursue a new career as an amateur cryptozoologist. They figured they didn’t need to tend the fields and be at the whim of the weather now that they’re set up from the inheritance, and they might as well put all these books and notes to use. Though most people in Grayce consider Titus eccentric, the reemergence of the Path River Peeler has lent them an air of credibility. For their part, Titus is basking in their newfound celebrity, delivering impromptu lectures about the Peeler in their home for fellow townspeople or engaging in long conversations at the market if someone brings up the Peeler.

When the PCs arrive at Titus’s house in town, they assume the PCs have come to question them about the Peeler. They invite the PCs inside, directing the party to a parlor where the bulk of their late uncle’s library is on display. Titus can tell the PCs any of the stories detailed in the Rumors in Grayce sidebar. If the PCs offer their own theory as to what the Peeler might be, Titus latches onto the idea, bending over backwards to incorporate the PC’s suggestion into their own wild speculations. A PC who succeeds at a DC 14 Perception check to Sense Motive recognizes that, while Titus might share their uncle’s enthusiasm for biology, but they have the perspective of a superstitious farmer, not a scientist.

PCs looking for reliable, hard facts about the Peeler must study the books and journals Titus has laid out in their parlor. A PC can study the books by making a DC 16 Academia Lore, Nature, or Occultism check. A PC can Aid on the check by succeeding at a DC 14 Diplomacy check either to enlist Titus’s help or simply keep the former farmer busy.

tiers.x: Treat a successful check as if the character had succeeded on a check to Recall Knowledge about the Peeler. For example, you might tell the players that the Peeler is inured to cold, or that the monster dislikes loud noises.
On a failure, the PCs uncover plenty of information about cryptids like the Peeler but learn nothing specific about the Peeler itself.

titus.title: Reward
titus.x: For studying Titus’s collection of books and journals, award the PCs 20 XP.

damarys.x: Ever since she was abandoned on the doorstep of the town’s temple to Andoletta, Damarys has been a thorn in Grayce’s side. Though Andoletta’s priests endeavored to raise her with love and attention, Damarys has always kept her distance from her community. She prefers to be left alone and goes out of her way to ensure she isn’t around when the town is looking for volunteers. When she does interact with others, it’s usually to make a biting criticism. More often, she simply lurks on the fringes of gatherings, fixing her fellow townspeople with a scornful stare. Infuriatingly, Damarys learned from a young age to always follow the rules just enough to avoid punishment. As a result, though everyone in town dislikes Damarys, no one can point to concrete proof of the mischief she’s suspected of.

Damarys’s cottage lies a few miles east of Grayce and roughly an hour’s walk north of Albin Derkensoor’s ranch. When the PCs arrive there, Damarys has just returned home from grazing her modest flock of sheep. She is a woman in her late 20s with a somewhat wild look, thanks to her patchwork clothes and the mismatched color of her eyes. Her tousled hair is woven with rodent skulls, iron nails, and other baubles, and her shepherd’s crook is made of willow wood: a lone holdover from her time spent at Andoletta’s temple. Damarys acknowledges the party’s approach with an unwelcoming nod.

Unlike the party’s other two leads (or anyone else in Grayce), Damarys has seen the Path River Peeler firsthand, but she’s not inclined to share what she knows. She believes that once the Peeler has finished its current killing spree, the monster will return to the Netherworld, allowing her to slip back through the rift alongside it. If a band of do-gooding adventurers kills the Peeler before then, she’ll miss her chance and be stuck in Grayce forever.

Despite her initial reluctance to speak with the party, clever PCs can play on Damarys’s contempt for the people of Grayce and trick her into revealing some information about the Peeler. Damarys is confident she’ll soon be leaving Grayce behind, and in the meantime feels the townspeople deserve whatever misery the Peeler brings. A PC can get Damarys talking with a successful DC 21 Deception check. Alternatively, a character can break the ice by noting either her occult baubles or her shepherd’s crook with a successful DC 18 Occultism or Religion check, respectively.

Once she gets started, Damarys’s disdain for the people of Grayce reveals itself. “They’re no better than these sheep,” Damarys says, “Dumb animals clamoring for safety, blind to the wonders that fill the Universe and worlds beyond.” If asked if she’s seen the Peeler, Damarys smirks. “Oh yes. Its touch carries with it the chill of the Netherworld. The Peeler will return home soon enough, but until then, you—and everyone else in Grayce—would be best to stay out of its way.”

At some point during the conversation with Damarys, make a secret DC 17 Perception check for each of the PCs. Any character who succeeds spots a flicker of movement as a tiny figure, its body seemingly made of twisted brambles, scuttles into the nearby bushes. The creature is named Mocking-Vain, a minor fey spirit that serves Damarys. If asked about the creature, Damarys simply nods. “As I said, the world outside of Grayce is filled with wonders—and terrors.” A character who succeeds at a DC 14 Nature check to Recall Knowledge identifies Mocking-Vain as a sprigjack.

damarys.title: Development
damarys.x: Damarys can share as much—or as little—information about the Path River Peeler as you’d like, but keep in mind that Damarys is only a bit more well-informed about magical matters than some of the PCs might be. Much of what she “knows” about the Peeler is speculation fueled by her hopes of leaving Grayce behind.

The PCs should leave the meeting with Damarys with the suspicion that she knows more about the Path River Peeler than she lets on. Throughout the encounter, she’s careful not to lie, instead smiling enigmatically if the PCs ask her a question she doesn’t want to answer. Though she might hint that the Peeler makes its lair somewhere in the Shivering Bluffs, she won’t reveal the exact location of the hags’ old cavern, Hag Hollow. If the PCs attack her, Damarys cowers and claims (truthfully, at this point) that she’s done nothing wrong. She fights back only if she feels her life’s in danger; if this occurs, Mocking-Vain also leaps to her defense. See area **A11** of Hag Hollow for statistics for both Damarys and Mocking-Vain, if needed.

Regardless of the outcome of the meeting, Damarys doesn’t want the PCs poking about in her business. That night, she sends the party a warning (see **Event 1: Grisly Delivery**), then retreats to Hag Hollow to alert her allies there.

damarys.title: Reward
damarys.x: For meeting with Damarys, reward the party 20 XP.

ranch.x: Having finished their preliminary investigation, the PCs can head to Albin Derkensoor’s ranch. When they arrive, Albin greets the party accompanied by his ranch hand, **Euphis** (superstitious male human laborer 0). Albin shows the PCs to the rooms he’s prepared for them in the main building, then gives them free rein of the rest of the grounds. If the characters seem uncertain about how to begin, Albin suggests two avenues of investigation: searching the sheep’s pen for clues and interviewing Euphis about the night he saw the Peeler.

**Searching the Pen:** Albin has been a successful rancher for decades, and even though he now leaves most of the work to hired hands, his flock of sheep remains several dozen strong. Albin’s sheep appear healthy, but the animals are clearly spooked, huddling together in one corner of the pen and bleating excitably as the PCs approach. A PC can attempt to calm the sheep by making a DC 14 Nature check to Command an Animal. On a success, the sheep settle and return to moving about the pen, though they still clearly avoid one end of the wooden enclosure.

A PC who Searches the pen can attempt a DC 14 Perception check. On a success, the character finds a set of unusual tracks in one corner of the pen. (If the PCs calmed the sheep, the tracks are in the area the flock continues to avoid. PCs who Search that area notice the tracks automatically.) The tracks are of a creature that walks upright like a human, but with long, thin toes like those of a primate.

A PC who succeeds at a DC 22 Stealth check to Track can follow the trail to the bottom of a 20-foot-high cliff about a mile north of Albin’s ranch (in the general direction of the Shivering Bluffs). The tracks disappear at this point, suggesting that the creature scrambled up the cliff on the way to wherever it was headed.

No matter how hard the characters search, they lose the Peeler’s trail here, though a character who makes a successful DC 14 Perception check discovers a growth of unusual black fungus nearby. The finger-like growths are cold to the touch and if harvested dissolve to oily slime within minutes. A character who succeeds at a DC 21 Nature check to Recall Knowledge identifies the growths as barrow claw, an extremely rare fungus said to be native to the Netherworld. (The Path River Peeler unknowingly deposited the barrow claw spores here on its flight from Albin’s ranch to Hag Hollow.)

**Interviewing Euphis:** Euphis is a kind-hearted human man in his late 20s, but his overactive imagination often leads to naivety. He’s worked for Albin for several years now, though he maintains vague hopes of becoming a soldier, or perhaps an adventurer like the PCs. He even keeps a battered shield and wooden sword beside his bed in one of the ranch’s outbuildings. On the night of the Peeler’s visit, Euphis was awakened to the sound of the sheep screaming in their pen. Grabbing his sword and shield, Euphis rushed to the yard and spotted the Peeler silhouetted in the moonlight. He began shouting and banging on his shield, driving off the Peeler with his racket before the monster could turns its attention on him.

Euphis caught only a brief glance of the Peeler, and his memories are confused by his active imagination. He variously describes the Peeler as a vampire, a bat-faced demon, and an ape-like creature akin to a black-furred yeti. Sorting out what Euphis really saw requires a DC 14 Diplomacy check. On a success, the PCs confirm the following.

items: The Peeler walked upright and was covered with bristly black fur. It had weirdly long fingers and saucer-like eyes that reflected the moonlight.
The Peeler clearly intending to harm the sheep, but when Euphis banged on his shield, the creature clasped its oversized ears and fled.
A chill lingered in the air even after the Peeler retreated, leaving Euphis shivering for several minutes. (In fairness, Euphis’s shivering was likely more due to fear than the chill.)

ranch.x: If the PCs happen to ask Euphis about Damarys, he knows the woman well, as the two of them shared their childhood at Andoletta’s temple. Like most people in town, Euphis doesn’t like Damarys, going so far as to accuse her of practicing sinister magics. Euphis recounts one night when they were teenagers, where he followed Damarys as she stole her way to the Shivering Bluffs. Once she spotted him, she turned into a raven and took flight. (Like many of his memories, Damarys’s transformation is a product of Euphis’s overactive imagination, though the seed of the story remains true.) If pressed, Euphis can tell a dozen more stories about times Damarys was mean to him or picked on him.

ranch.title: Development
ranch.x: There’s nothing more to be discovered at the ranch. As the stake-out spot Jarelle identified is a day’s walk away, Albin suggests the PCs rest for the night before heading out the next morning.

ranch.title: Reward
ranch.x: For investigating Albin’s ranch, grant the party 20 XP. Reward the PCs an additional 20 XP if they discover and correctly identify the barrow claw fungus.

event1.x: Whether the PCs rest at Albin’s ranch or somewhere back in town, that night they receive an unsettling delivery. If the characters think to set a watch, whichever PC is awake at midnight can attempt a DC 14 Perception check. On a success, they hear a shuffling noise outside their door, followed by the sound of receding footsteps. A character who rushes to the door arrives in time to spot a hooded figure retreating into the night.

A PC can run down the fleeing figure by succeeding at a DC 16 Acrobatics or Athletics check. On a failure, Euphis tackles the figure in the yard instead (if the PCs are resting in town, a different bystander waylays the figure). Once their hood is removed, the figure is revealed to be a local youth named **Lev Urada** (stubborn male human punk 0). Lev snarls and struggles to escape but eventually relents, knowing he’s been caught.

Outside the PCs’ door lies a halfling-sized bundle wrapped in a heavy blanket. Unwrapping the bundle reveals a freshly peeled sheepskin, still wet with blood. This grisly delivery is from Damarys, who gave Lev a few coins to deliver the package in hopes of dissuading the party from further investigations.

Lev fears and idolizes Damarys in equal measure. The PCs must succeed at a DC 14 Intimidation check to Coerce him into revealing where he got the sheepskin. If the PCs bring the matter to the town guard, the authorities are sympathetic but admit there’s not much they can do: Unless the PCs can prove Damarys stole the sheep from which the skin was taken, she hasn’t broken any law. If the PCs head to Damarys’s cottage to confront her there, they find her cottage empty, though the skinless body of the sheep (which was, indeed, was taken from her own flock) hangs from a tree out back.

event1.title: Reward
event1.x: Award the party 20 XP for discovering the source of the bloody sheepskin, either by interrogating Lev or by visiting Damarys’s cottage.

bluffs.x: A hard-beaten livestock path winds its way through the hills east of Grayce to the location Jarelle identified as the most likely place to encounter the Path River Peeler. Local shepherds graze their flocks here, but they’ve been avoiding the area in recent days due to everyone being on edge about the Peeler sightings. Walking there (either from Grayce or Albin’s ranch) takes most of the day. Along the way, the PCs pass by pastures where the sheep of Grayce graze, but other than the occasional meeting with a shepherd and their flock, the journey is uneventful. Once they arrive, the PCs can make camp atop the hill Jarelle identified, giving them a clear view of the surrounding countryside—and a beautiful sunset.

A few hours after sunset, the silence is broken by an unnerving cackle that echoes across the hills. As the PCs search for the laughter’s source, each of them can attempt a DC 14 Perception check to Seek. Any character who succeeds spots a dark figure near a copse of trees a few hundred yards from their campsite. The night is too dark to make out many details, but the figure seems to be covered in animal fur, though it stands upright like a humanoid. As soon as the PCs move in its direction, the figure bolts and disappears into the trees.

chase.x: Event 2: Countryside Chase

The figure the PCs spotted is Jarelle’s sister, Phara, who has dressed up in a homemade Peeler costume for a bit of fun at the party’s expense. Chasing down Phara uses the chase rules found on page 192 of *Pathfinder GM Core*. Phara starts the chase one obstacle ahead of the PCs and moves at a pace of one obstacle each round. The chase ends when the PCs catch up to Phara, or once Phara reaches the chase’s final obstacle. Remember that if the PCs successfully helped Jarelle identify this location, each of them gains a +1 circumstance bonus to checks made to overcome obstacles during the chase.
Keep Pace · Obstacle 2
**Chase Points** 3; **Overcome** DC 12 Acrobatics or Athletics to maintain pace with the fleeing figure, DC 16 Perception to keep the figure in sight
The shadowy figure breaks away, threatening to escape into the night. As the PCs bound down the hillside, they must watch their footing to avoid a nasty tumble.
Overgrown Forest · Obstacle 2
**Chase Points** 2; **Overcome** DC 16 Perception to avoid becoming lost in the lightless woods, DC 12 Survival to spot the clearest route through the vegetation
The copse of trees at the bottom of the hill is overgrown with briars.
Crossing the Gully · Obstacle 2
**Chase Points** 2; **Overcome** DC 12 Acrobatics to use the fallen tree like a balance beam, DC 16 Athletics to leap across the gully
Rainwater from the bluffs has cut a gully through this part of the woods. An uprooted tree spans the gap.
Find the Trail · Obstacle 2
**Chase Points** 3; **Overcome** DC 12 Survival to pick up the figure’s trail, DC 16 Perception to spot a tuft of fur left behind from Phara’s costume
As the PCs emerge from the forest, they find themselves at the foot of the Shivering Bluffs. Picking up the figure’s trail from here requires keen eyes.
After the Chase

If the PCs catch up with Phara, she begs for mercy as soon as the characters unmask her. She admits to stitching together the Peeler costume from the odd animal pelts, then hiding in the nearby trees to wait for the PCs to arrive. She only wanted to have a little fun, she explains, and can’t suppress a mischievous grin when she recalls the chase. “You should’ve seen the looks on all your faces!”

If the PCs fail to catch Phara, they instead find her costume a short distance from the entrance to Hag Hollow, where she discarded it before heading back to town. In this case, the figure’s identity remains a mystery, though at your discretion Phara might admit to the prank later, after the PCs return to town.

chase.title: Development
chase.x: Regardless of when (or if) the PCs catch up to Phara, moments after the chase ends, another cackle pierces the night. Unlike the laughter they heard previously, the PCs are certain no mortal could reproduce this sound. In fact, the laughter is the otherworldly cry of the real Path River Peeler, returning to its lair after another successful hunt. If the PCs caught up with Phara at the Find the Trail obstacle, the sound comes from just over the nearest hill. Otherwise, the laughter continues long enough to lead the PCs to the entrance of Hag Hollow (area **A1**).

If Phara is with the PCs when they hear the Peeler’s cry, her eyes go wide at the sound. Assuming the PCs send her home while they investigate the laughter’s source, Phara readily agrees, this time without a hint of protest.

chase.title: Reward
chase.x: Award the PCs 60 XP if they successfully chase down Phara.

hollow.x: Hag Hollow is just one of the many natural cave systems that riddle the bluffs along the Path River. After the hags that once inhabited the caverns were driven away, the site sat empty for centuries, until Damarys’s voices led her to the location. Since then, Damarys has visited Hag Hollow regularly, enjoying the solitude the caves afford. A few years ago, a tribe of kobolds called the Shiverscales also happened upon the caves. At first, Damarys disliked the Shiverscales, but she agreed to let them stay after they promised to guard the caverns in her absence. The fact that the Shiverscales have come to regard the Path River Peeler as a sort of patron spirit has only endeared the kobolds to her further.

In addition to Damarys and the Shiverscales, two other groups of creatures inhabit Hag Hollow. The first is a band of sprigjacks lead by Damarys’s minion Mocking-Vain. The sprigjacks actually predate Damarys’s arrival at Hag Hollow, though they’ve since accepted the reclusive woman as the true holder of the caves. The second group is a pair of fungus leshies drawn by the barrow claw fungus that infests the caverns. Though the Shiverscales, the sprigjacks, and the leshies are all loyal to Damarys (and, through her, the Path River Peeler), the three groups generally avoid each other. None of them have ever crossed the chasm (area **A5**) that separates their lairs from the deepest parts of the caverns (areas **A10–A12**).

Of course, the Path River Peeler also lives within Hag Hollow. Every generation or so, the rift in area **A12** opens wide enough for the Peeler to enter the Universe. During these times, the Peeler haunts the countryside until the rift begins to close again, at which point the monster returns home to the Netherworld. While in the Universe, the Peeler usually comes and goes from Hag Hollow via a second tunnel that opens onto the surface about a half mile away (see area **A12**).

Hag Hollow is a natural cave system with walls and floors worn smooth by centuries of inhabitance. Unless noted otherwise, the ceilings of the caverns are 10 feet high, while those of passageways are 7 feet high. All areas are unlit, except for area **A11**, where Damarys’s campfire fills the area with dim light. The temperature throughout the caverns is unnaturally cold—not quite enough to freeze skin, but cold enough to frost one’s breath.

When the PCs arrive, Damarys is in area **A11**, having retreated to the caverns shortly after the PCs visited her. If the PCs didn’t meet with Damarys, she’s still in **A11**, but none of the inhabitants of Hag Hollow are on alert for intruders. In this case, you might decide to give the PCs a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative until the party’s presence in the caverns becomes obvious.

x: A footpath winds its way to the base of a cliff before disappearing into a low, dark cave. Boulders and thorny bushes line the path.

a1.x: Though the Path River Peeler typically enters Hag Hollow from another direction (see area **A12**), this entrance is where both Damarys and the Shiverscale kobolds come and go from the caves. The brush, boulders, and shape of the cliff face explain why Hag Hollow has remained largely unexplored for centuries; from any distance of more than 100 feet or so, the entrance is entirely unnoticeable.

**Creatures:** A group of four sprigjacks—subordinates of Damarys’s minion Mocking-Vain—lurk in the bushes just outside the entrance to the caves. The sprigjacks wait until the PCs approach the cave entrance before leaping from the thorns to attack.

a1.note: Four sprigjacks hide in the bushes outside the cave. They wait until the heroes approach the entrance. Then they leap from the thorns and attack.

a1.x: The adventure does not print this stat block. Use *Pathfinder Monster Core* 332.

x: Inside the cliff face, the footpath continues, snaking between walls of smooth but natural stone.

a2.x: **Hazards:** At the two points marked on the map, tripwires span the tunnel low to the ground. If the PCs notice the wires, they can step over them easily. Otherwise, passing through either area causes a lattice of tree branches and wooden spikes to snap shut across the passageway.

a2.name: Spiked Walls (2) · Hazard 1
a2.x: *Mechanical · Trap*. **Stealth** DC 15 (trained) to spot the trip wire. **Description** A low trip wire connects to a lattice panel covered with wooden spikes.
dcs: Disable DC 15 Thievery (trained) to snip the trip wire or jam the panel
Hardness 5; HP 24 (BT 12); Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; Weaknesses slashing 2

Spiked Wall (reaction) Trigger A creature triggers the trip wire; Effect A lattice panel lashed with wooden spikes swings shut across the passage. The triggering creature takes 3d6 piercing damage (DC 17 basic Reflex save). The panel provides lesser cover and prevents movement along the passage. The panel can be pushed open like a door with an Interact action, but it swings shut again unless wedged open with a heavy object.

a2.x: **Creature:** The area where the tunnel widens is used as an impromptu workshop by Crumbrunk, a mischievous jinkin whom the Shiverscale kobolds grudgingly adopted after Crumbrunk was exiled from his own gremlin clan. The Shiverscales don’t particularly like Crumbrunk, but they admit his traps are even more clever than the ones they could build themselves. If the PCs trigger his spiked wall traps, Crumbrunk crouches behind the boulder in the center of his workshop and peppers characters who are caught in the trapped section of the tunnel with blowgun darts. The boulder grants Crumbrunk standard cover, or greater cover if he uses the Take Cover action.

a2.note: Crumbrunk acts if the heroes trigger a spiked wall. He crouches behind the boulder in his workshop. He shoots darts at anyone caught in the trapped tunnel. The boulder gives him standard cover, or greater cover if he Takes Cover. Three of his ten darts carry giant viper venom. If the heroes avoid or beat the traps he shouts to alert the kobolds in A3.

a2.x: **Items** blowgun (10 darts, 3 of which are coated with giant viper venom), shortsword
**Ranged** (one action) blowgun +9 (agile, nonlethal, range increment 20 feet, reload 1), **Damage** 1 piercing plus giant viper venom
**Giant Viper Venom** (poison) **Saving Throw** DC 17 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 1d6 poison damage (1 round); **Stage 2** 1d6 poison damage and drained 1 (1 round)
The adventure prints only these lines for Crumbrunk. Use the jinkin in *Pathfinder Monster Core* 181 for AC, HP, saves, Speed and other abilities.

a2.title: Development
a2.x: If the PCs avoid or overcome his spiked wall traps, Crumbrunk shouts to alert the kobolds to the northwest. If alerted, the Shiverscales don’t come to Crumbrunk’s aid, but rather position themselves to ambush the characters when they arrive in area **A3**.

If captured, Crumbrunk can be Coerced into telling the PCs more about Hag Hollow, including information about its current inhabitants and the general layout of the caverns. If asked about his own history, Crumbrunk explains his fellow gremlins cast him out after one of his traps malfunctioned and injured their leader. The PCs might encounter these gremlins in “Sabotage!,” also in this adventure anthology.

a2.title: Treasure
a2.x: Crumbrunk’s trap making tools function as an artisan’s toolkit worth 4 gp. Among the scattered tools is a thin glass vial that contains a lesser antidote.

x: This cavern is shaped roughly like a figure eight, with two smaller, circular caves joined in the center of the area. Pillars of natural stone stretch from floor to ceiling in each of these smaller caves. The ground near the base of the pillars is crowded with straw pallets, bedrolls, and the remnants of campfires. In the northern cave, rough stairs rise to the north, while another set of steps rises westward from the southern area. Tunnels stretch to the east from both the northern and southern caves.

a3.x: The rank-and-file members of the Shiverscale tribe gather in this area. Their leader Zurkurk (area **A7**) occasionally visits to address them; otherwise, the kobolds spend their time sleeping, eating, or harassing Crumbrunk in area **A2**.

**Creatures:** Four Shiverscale kobolds are in this area when the PCs arrive at Hag Hollow. If they hear sounds of combat in area **A2**, two kobolds each hide behind the pillars to the north and south, ambushing the PCs as they enter the cave. The kobolds consider this a brilliant “pincer maneuver,” but they haven’t thought the tactic through. If any of them rolls a critical failure with their crossbow and at least one of their allies in the opposite cave is a possible target, roll a DC 15 flat check. On a failure, the bolt hits another kobold.

a3.note: Four kobolds. If they heard combat in A2, two hide behind the north pillars and two behind the south pillars. They ambush the heroes as they enter. On a critical failure with a crossbow, roll a DC 15 flat check if an ally in the opposite cave is a possible target. On a failure the bolt hits another kobold. All have sneak attack so do 1d4 extra damage to off guard. Loud noise here alerts Zoti in A4 and the bodyguards in A6.

a3.x: **Melee** (one action) shortsword +7 (agile, finesse, versatile S), **Damage** 1d6+3 piercing
**Ranged** (one action) crossbow +7 (range increment 120 feet, reload 1), **Damage** 1d8+2 piercing

**Sneak Attack** The Shiverscale kobold deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to off-guard creatures.

a3.x: Loud noises in this area alert the tribe’s gecko wrangler, Zoti, in area **A4**, as well as Zurkurk’s bodyguards in area **A6**. Neither group comes to investigate the sounds, but they prepare themselves for battle, as described in those areas.

a3.x: In addition to their weapons and armor, one of the kobolds has hidden a pouch containing seven agates worth 1 gp beneath their bedroll.

x: This oval-shaped grotto reeks of animal waste. In the southern wall, a recessed shelf appears to have been adapted as a sleeping space. The cavern’s floor drops into a chasm to the northwest.

a4.x: Zoti, the Shiverscales’ gecko wrangler, has used her seniority to take over this cavern as her living space. She spends most of her time here training her giant gecko, Big Eye, but as the tribe’s eldest member, she occasionally visits area **A7** to advise her son, Zurkurk.

**Creatures:** If she hears sounds of combat in area **A3**, Zoti sends Big Eye to the ceiling just above the cavern’s entrance and prepares herself for battle. Otherwise, Zoti rests in the alcove in the southern wall and must spend her first turn gathering up her spear and shield. Meanwhile, Big Eye clings to the stone just beneath the lip of the chasm to the northwest.

a4.note: If Zoti heard combat in A3, Big Eye waits on the ceiling above the entrance and Zoti is ready. Otherwise Zoti rests in the south alcove. She spends her first turn gathering her spear and shield. Big Eye then clings just under the lip of the chasm to the northwest. Zoti has sneak attack so does 1d4 extra damage to off guard.

a4.title: Development
a4.x: Characters standing near the ledge to the northwest see the entrance to another cave (area **A10**) on the far side of the chasm. The chasm is 15 feet wide at this point, but the party could cross the distance using a grappling hook and rope or by constructing a bridge using the materials in area **A8**. The chasm’s walls have a Climb DC of 15. See area **A5** for a full description of the chasm.

a4.title: Treasure
a4.x: Zoti’s sleeping shelf is filled with heavy winter blankets and foul-smelling animal furs. Beneath the assorted bedding is a *gecko potion*.

x: A chasm winds through the center of this cavern like a lazy river. In most places, the chasm is twenty feet across, though it narrows to half that distance in some spaces. Forty feet above the chasm’s floor, a ledge of natural stone wraps around the cavern’s eastern end, forming a walkway that connects the chasm’s northern and southern sides. The cavern’s ceiling rises another twenty feet above this ledge, its soaring vault transforming even the slightest sound made in the cavern into a chorus of echoes.

a5.x: Due to the echoes, creatures in this area take a –2 circumstance penalty to Stealth checks made to Sneak and gain weakness 2 to sonic damage.

This cavern serves as a natural barrier between the areas to the south and the caves used by the coven of hags centuries ago (areas **A11–A12**). Only Damarys crosses the chasm regularly, walking along the ledge at the east end of the cavern. The Shiverscale kobolds are too frightened to venture past the chasm, and the Path River Peeler dislikes the echoes the cavern’s high ceiling creates. (If the PCs retreat here during the encounter with the Peeler in area **A12**, the monster pursues them as far as the ledge south of area **A11**, but no further.)

**Navigating the Chasm:** Depending on where the PCs enter this area, they should be able to see several exits from the chamber, including the tunnels to areas **A5**, **A9**, **A10**, and **A11**. The mouth of a wide cavern overlooks the chasm at area **A4**. Finally, a cramped tunnel opens onto the chasm’s floor from area **A8**. This opening is hidden from the ledge, but characters on the ground can find it with a successful DC 14 Perception check to Search.

Though it is barely 5 feet wide, the natural ledge that circles the cavern is stable, save for the 10-foot-square section outside the tunnel to area **A3**. See the Hazard section below for details about this unstable overlook.

The ledge south of area **A11** is only 10 feet from the ledge on the opposite side of the chasm, meaning characters could conceivably Leap the gap. Alternatively, the party can cross the distance using a grappling hook and rope or by constructing a bridge using the materials in area **A8**. Of course, the PCs could also Climb down the cavern’s walls, cross the bottom of the chasm on foot, and Climb up the opposite side. The chasm’s walls have a Climb DC of 15.
**Hazard:** The jinkin Crumbrunk (area **A2**) has prepared this natural ledge to collapse. Though the Shiverscales and Damarys know how to avoid the weakened area, the PCs might not be so lucky.

Collapse (reaction) Trigger A Small or larger creature moves onto the weakened section of the overlook; Effect The ledge collapses. Any creature on the ledge that fails to Grab an Edge (DC 20) plummets 40 feet into the chasm below.

a5.x: **Creatures:** A few decades ago, a wandering ogre discovered Hag Hollow but slipped and fell as he edged along the chasm’s ledge. The ogre’s remains—animated by the presence of the rift to the Netherworld in area **A12**—patrols the chasm’s floor.

a5.note: The skeletal ogre patrols the chasm floor, 40 feet below the ledge. Everyone here takes a –2 penalty to Sneak. Everyone here gains weakness 2 to sonic.

x: Three column-like formations of limestone support the twenty-foot-high ceiling of this cavern. Crude paintings of kobolds kneeling before a towering, demon-like figure decorate the cavern’s walls. A tattered curtain separates the main space from an alcove in the cavern’s southwest corner.

a7.x: The leader of the Shiverscales, a kobold cavern mage named Zurkurk, led his tribe to the Shivering Bluffs several years ago. When they encountered Damarys in Hag Hollow, Zurkurk arranged a truce by swearing his tribe’s allegiance to the changeling. Zurkurk’s true loyalty, however, lies with the Path River Peeler. Though he’s only seen the monster once or twice, Zurkurk is convinced the Peeler is a devil from Hell and hopes one day to bargain with the fiend for magical power. In the meantime, he spends his days painting fanciful depictions of the Peeler on the walls.

**Cave Paintings:** Zurkurk’s paintings don’t give the PCs a much clearer picture of the Peeler than the descriptions they collected back in Grayce. In these images, the Peeler is an ape-like creature with black claws that stretch nearly to its feet. If the scale of Zurkurk’s paintings could be trusted, the Peeler would stand nearly 20 feet tall—however, this is more a product of the kobold’s reverence for the creature, rather than an accurate representation of its size. (While far taller than a kobold, the Peeler is only about 6 feet tall.)
One detail Zurkurk managed to capture across all the paintings are the Peeler’s unusual, oversized ears. Insightful PCs might take this as another clue that the Peeler is sensitive to loud noises.

**Creature:** If the PCs haven’t encountered him elsewhere, they find the kobold here working on his latest painting on the cavern’s southern wall. If hard pressed, Zurkurk casts *invisibility* on himself and flees up the passage to area **A9**, hoping his pursuers tumble into the pit trap in area **A8**.

a7.note: Zurkurk is here only if the heroes have not met him elsewhere. He is painting on the southern wall. If hard pressed he casts invisibility and flees up the passage to A9. He hopes pursuers fall into the pit trap in A8.

a7.x: The alcove behind the curtain to the southwest conceals Zurkurk’s sleeping space. Blankets and animal pelts crowd the alcove. A shelf carved into the wall holds Zurkurk’s collection of brushes and paints, as well the entirety of the Shiverscales’ wealth: a pouch containing 80 sp and 32 gp, a collection of four *minor healing potions*, and an ivory walrus tusk worth 10 gp.

a8.x: The tunnel turns at a nearly 90 degree angle as it leads toward the lair of dangerous fungus leshies. This bend is a perfect spot to set a trap for any potential invaders.

**Hazard:** Crumbrunk, the jinkin trap maker from area **A2**, recently dug a pit trap in the middle of this passageway. The Shiverscales and Damarys avoid the trap by sliding wooden planks across the pit. Stacks of these 10-foot-long planks rest against the walls to the east and west of the pit.

a8.x: **Creature:** A giant viper lives at the bottom of the pit. Crumbrunk occasionally harvests the viper’s venom, which the jinkin uses to coat his blowgun darts. The viper attacks any creature that falls into the pit.

a8.note: The giant viper lives at the bottom of the pit. It attacks any creature that falls in.

**Crawlway:** A tunnel with a low ceiling at the lowest part of this area slopes downwards 20 feet to the bottom of the chasm in area **A5**. Medium or smaller creatures must Crawl down the passage and larger creatures must Squeeze. This end of the tunnel is obvious, but characters in the chasm must succeed at a DC 14 Perception check to Search to notice it.

a8.title: Development
a8.x: With 10 minutes of work and a successful DC 16 Crafting check, a PC can use the wooden planks to build a bridge across the chasm in area **A5**.

x: The air inside this cave is even colder than elsewhere in the caverns. Black fungi shaped eerily like human fingers grow along the southern wall. A tunnel leads into the cave from the west, while a set of natural stairs turns sharply to the north.

a9.x: The fungus is identical to what the PCs might have discovered while following the Peeler’s trail from Albin Derkensoor’s ranch. A character who succeeds at a DC 21 Nature check to Recall Knowledge can identify the fungus as barrow claw. The fungus is cold to the touch and quickly dissolves into oily slime if harvested. If allowed to spread, barrow claw can be a blight to crops, but it is otherwise harmless to animals and other creatures.

**Creatures:** When the rift from the Netherworld opened in area **A12**, the Path River Peeler unknowingly transported spores of barrow claw fungus here. The spores found purchase along the southern wall and eventually drew a pair of fungus leshies to the area. When the PCs enter the cave, the leshies have used their Change Shape ability to blend into the patches of barrow claw. The leshies remain in their fungus form unless the PCs disturb the barrow claw, at which point they return to their true shapes and attack. The leshies fight to the death, but they don’t pursue characters who flee beyond the cavern.

a9.note: Two leshies hide as patches of barrow claw. They stay in fungus form unless the heroes disturb the barrow claw. Then they change back and attack. They fight to the death. They do not pursue heroes who flee the cavern.

a9.x: The adventure prints only these lines. Use the fungus leshy in *Pathfinder Monster Core* 217 for everything else.

a10.x: The entrance to this cave is hidden from most parts of area **A5**, although creatures standing at the westernmost end of the ledge above the chasm can see it, as can creatures in area **A4**. The PCs can reach the cave by shimmying across the chasm or by Climbing the chasm’s walls, as described in area **A5**.

Nearly a century ago, a brave (but somewhat hapless) human swashbuckler named Klerran Keel discovered Hag Hollow and decided to explore the caverns. He made camp in this out-of-the-way cave, but before going to sleep he blew his bugle across the chasm, tickled by the echoes the call made. The racket disturbed the Path River Peeler, who crept into the hidden cave and killed Klerran while he slept.

a10.title: Treasure
a10.x: If the PCs make their way into the cave, they discover Klerran’s bones in a heap against the northern wall. Bloodstains on Klerran’s buckler suggest the man died of violence, though his rapier still rests inside its sheath nearby. Klerran’s pack has mostly rotted away, but among the scraps of leather the PCs can turn up his fateful bugle (a virtuoso musical instrument), as well as a *vagabond’s teapot* (page 118).

a10.title: Development
a10.x: A PC who blows Klerran’s bugle when they encounter the Path River Peeler in area **A12** gains a +1 item bonus on Intimidation checks to Demoralize the monster.

a10.title: Reward
a10.x: Award the PCs 60 XP if they discover Klerran’s remains.

x: The walls of this cavern rise to form a dome nearly twenty feet above the cavern’s floor. Six pillars made of natural stone—but spaced too evenly to have occurred by chance—form a ring in the center of the space. Scratched into the cavern’s walls are hundreds of strange symbols; while some are simple stick figures, others seem to bear occult significance.
Beneath the carvings grow patches of black fungus shaped like human fingers. A tunnel leads into the area from the southeast, while a set of natural stone stairs exits downward to the east.

a11.x: In centuries past, the hags that once inhabited Hag Hollow gathered in this cave to commune with one another and share foul magics. This includes the original ritual they used to open the portal to the Netherworld in area **A12**. The voices Damarys hears are loudest here, and this is where she often comes when she visits the Shivering Bluffs. The pillars in the center of the cave were indeed shaped by magic, though they have no magical properties now. The black fungus is barrow claw, identical to the patches the PCs might have encountered in area **A9** or near Albin’s ranch.

**Creatures:** Once she finished with the sheepskin Lev Urada delivered to the party in **Event 1**, Damarys headed to the Shivering Bluffs just in case the PCs found their way to Hag Hollow. When the PCs arrive, she stands beside a campfire inside the ring of pillars, while Mocking-Vain lurks in the shadows nearby.

Damarys believes (correctly) that if the PCs kill the Path River Peeler, the rift to the Netherworld will be closed forever. As a result, she tries to prevent the party from entering area **A12**. She gives the PCs one last chance to head back to Grayce. She starts off defiant, telling them that the caves are hers and they are intruding on her property, thinking that appealing to possessions might gain some traction with the adventurers. If they don’t listen to that approach, she pleads for them to leave, saying that her destiny is in these caves and the PCs are ruining her chance at destiny. If that approach doesn’t seem to work, she offers to tell them everything she knows about Hag Hollow, the Path River Peeler, and her supposed role in all this. She hopes they will be reasonable and understand things from her perspective, but by this point thinks its probably hopeless for them to understand. If they continue to refuse to leave, she attacks, opening combat by casting *stupefy* on the most likely spellcasters.

**Carvings:** The symbols on the walls were carved over generations by the hags who once inhabited the caverns. Most of the symbols are meaningless, but a character who studies the carvings for 10 minutes and succeeds at a DC 15 Occultism or DC 18 Arcana, Nature, or Religion check gains a +1 circumstance bonus on checks made to seal the nether rift hazard in area **A12**.

a11.title: Treasure
a11.x: Among the carvings is a stylized image of a cat that any character trained in Occultism recognizes as an ancient symbol of protection. The image is etched into the wall, but the characters can chip it away with a minute of work. Once separated from the stone, the symbol functions as a *jade cat talisman*.
In addition to her armor and weapons, Damarys wears a *ring of sigils*.

a12.x: The ceiling of this cavern is 20 feet high. The area is dark, but a crooked line of blue light glows in the middle of the northern wall. The light emanates from the rift to the Netherworld in that area and is visible from either entrance to the cave.

x: A layer of crystalline frost covers every surface of this oddly shaped cavern. The source of the frost is obvious: a chill breeze blows from a scar in the middle of the cavern’s northern wall, filling the area with gently drifting snowflakes. The fissure is only a thumb’s width across, but a pale blue light glows within it, visible even in the darkness.
Patches of black fungus, each roughly ten feet in diameter, grow throughout the cavern. Steps lead up into the area from the west, while another set of stairs rises to the east.

a12.x: Working together, the hags that once inhabited Hag Hollow created this portal to the Netherworld. The portal opens infrequently—sometimes remaining shut for a decade or more—but when it does, the Path River Peeler finds its way into the Universe. Once it arrives, the Peeler hunts the area along the Path River until some unnamed force bids it to return, at which point the portal widens enough for the Peeler to pass back through it. Damarys hopes to accompany the Peeler the next time this occurs, but for now she must wait, as the Path River Peeler’s hunger remains unsated.

**Creature:** Shortly after the PCs enter the area, a deep, ominous cackle (identical to the one the characters heard outside Hag Hollow) echoes down the stairwell to the east. Moments later, the Path River Peeler emerges, having just returned from its most recent hunt. Clutched within the monster’s claws is the body of a sheep—not flayed entirely of skin but certainly ravaged and still dripping with fresh blood. When it notices the PCs, the Peeler tosses the carcass aside and unleashes its Otherworldly Cry.

In combat, the Peeler makes claw Strikes against the closest PC. If the characters successfully Demoralize it, the Peeler uses its Flight Response reaction to scuttle up the cavern’s walls. It then uses Blood Run Cold against the PC that Demoralized it before returning to melee. The Peeler is immune to the effects of the nether rift hazard.

a12.note: The Peeler enters from the east stairs shortly after the heroes arrive. It opens with Otherworldly Cry. It claws the closest hero. If Demoralized it uses Flight Response to scuttle up the walls. It then uses Blood Run Cold on the hero who Demoralized it and returns to melee. The Peeler is immune to the nether rift hazard. The rift's wind triggers when the Peeler enters and the hazard then rolls initiative. Klerran's bugle gives +1 item bonus to Demoralize the Peeler. If the heroes retreat, the Peeler follows only as far as the ledge south of A11. If the rift is disabled first, the Peeler becomes clumsy 1 and gains weakness 5 to all damage except cold.

a12.x: The adventure does not print this stat block. Use the Path River Peeler stat block on page 123 of *Troubles in Grayce* (Adventure Toolbox), which is outside the pages supplied.

**Hazard:** When the Peeler appears, a gust of icy wind blasts from the portal to the Netherworld. The gust causes the temperature in the cavern to drop even further; in response, the barrow claw fungi throughout the area release their spores.

a12.name: Nether Rift · Hazard 3
a12.x: *Unique · Complex · Magical · Shadow · Trap*. **Stealth** +5 (trained). **Description** A chill wind blows from a fissure in the cavern wall.
dcs: Disable DC 18 Arcana, Nature, Occultism, or Religion (trained) to seal the rift, three successes total; or dispel magic (3rd rank; counteract DC 17)
Barrow Claw HP 44 (BT 22); Immunities cold, critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; Weaknesses fire 5

Wind from the Netherworld (reaction) (cold, shadow) Trigger The Path River Peeler enters the cave; Effect A gust of ice-cold wind from the Netherworld blasts from the rift in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in the area take 2d4 cold damage (DC 20 basic Fortitude save). The hazard then rolls initiative.

Routine (2 actions) The hazard uses its first action to repeat its Wind from the Netherworld reaction. If any patch of barrow claw remains, one of the patches chosen by the GM releases a cloud of spores. The spores fill the barrow claw’s space and last until the beginning of the hazard’s next turn. Creatures within the spores become concealed, and all creature outside the spores become concealed to creatures within it. A creature that enters the spores or starts their turn in the area takes 1d6 persistent cold damage until they brush off the spores as an Interact action.
Reset The rift reopens after 2d10 years. Killing the Path River Peeler permanently seals the rift.

a12.title: Development
a12.x: If the PCs kill the Path River Peeler, the rift to the Netherworld snaps shut, leaving behind no evidence that it was ever there. If the PCs disable the hazard before the Peeler is defeated, the monster howls in rage as its connection to the Netherworld is severed. Until the portal is opened again (an event that won’t occur until long after the adventure has ended), the Peeler becomes clumsy 1 and gains weakness 5 to all damage except cold.

The tunnel from which the Peeler entered meanders for about half a mile before opening onto the surface. Unless you want to expand the adventure by introducing additional encounter areas, this secondary entrance to Hag Hollow is unremarkable.

conclusion.x: Having defeated the Path River Peeler and closing the rift to the Netherworld, the PCs can return to Grayce as heroes. If they think to bring the Peeler with them, a crowd of townspeople quickly gathers to gawk at the alien-looking corpse. Titus Horvat, the farmer turned cryptozoologist, even offers the party a sum of 60 gp in exchange for the beast. Despite Titus’s best efforts to preserve its remains, the Peeler’s flesh rots unnaturally fast over the next few days, though the monster’s skeleton remains on display in their parlor for years to come.

As for Damarys, no one in Grayce celebrates her death, but her reluctance to help anyone but herself means she’s not missed. Her body is buried with little ceremony in the town’s smaller, new graveyard. The question of whether Damarys’s voices were only in her head, or if they truly were the whispers of the hags, remains unanswered. Perhaps one or more of the hags escaped extinction by fleeing through the rift and still plots revenge from their new home in the Netherworld. It’s possible Larmine, from the adventure “Sweet Tooth,” was drawn to the area due to this strong presence and past hag activity, and she might not be the last hag to visit and prey upon the area!
